verdict.rationale: The desktop client's source is publicly readable on GitHub (anyproto/anytype-ts), so the reading part of the story is met. However, two independent community reports say the repo's license is source-available rather than open source under the Open Source Definition, so the open-license part is not satisfied for the core app. The pack contains no first-party claim that the app itself is OSI-open; only the separate agents toolkit is called open-source. Missing for 10: an OSI-approved open license on the core app source, and first-party documentation of the license terms.
